entries.english:
XIV. Herzog Heinrich I. von Schlesien grants Themo the town of Naumburg on the Queis to establish under German law. 11 November 1233. From a certification made by the magistrate of Löwenberg on 27 August 1733, copied from the original, of the certification by Heinrich von Rosenberg, captain of the principalities of Schweidnitz and Jauer, dated 18 December 1445.

In the name of Jesus Christ, amen. What is done in time tends to fade from human memory with the passage of time unless it is strengthened in writing or by the testimony of witnesses. Therefore we, Heinrich, by the grace of God Duke of Kraków and Silesia, make known to all people of the present and future who see this charter that we have granted Themo the town of Naumburg to be settled under German law, the same law by which Löwenberg was granted its privileges. We graciously grant exemption from rents and services for twelve years and from tolls for six years, according to the terms of Crossen and Löwenberg. In addition, we grant the aforesaid town, together with the higher court, these villages: Bertoldisdorf, Thiemendorf, Seifersdorf, Giesmannsdorf, Herzogswalde, the village of Hugisdorf, Paritz, Hermansdorf, the village of Laurentiae, Birkenbrück, and the village called Zabuloth; moreover, eight manses and one meadow for pasture for livestock. We have also granted the aforesaid Themo the hereditary right to the office of schultheiß there, at two mills, the first of which he shall build to our one-third share, as he and his heirs, or anyone to whom he may later wish to sell it, see fit. So that this grant may remain inviolable forever, we have strengthened this charter with the impression of our seal. Done at Wrocław on the feast of Saint Martin, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1233, in the presence of Heinrich, parish priest of Novoforo; Konrad, scholasticus of Głogów; Hermann, parish priest of Auro; and the knights Merboto, Albert son of Bero, Godfrey the Bavarian, Heinrich the schultheiß of Novoforo, and many others.

1) The town of Crossen on the Oder, commonly called Crosten in the fifteenth century. 2) Berthelsdorf on the Queis, about one and a half miles east of Lauban. 3) Thiemendorf, about one mile east of Lauban. 4) Seifersdorf, about two and a half miles southwest of Bunzlau. 5) Giesmannsdorf, two miles south-southwest of Bunzlau. 6) Herzogswalde, immediately southeast of Naumburg on the Queis. 7) Silesian Haugsdorf on the Queis, above Naumburg. 8) Paritz, half a mile west-southwest of Bunzlau. 9) Probably Hermansdorf, also called Herrnsdorf, three quarters of a mile west-southwest of Bunzlau, formerly belonging to the convent of nuns at Naumburg. 10) Lorenzdorf, also called Lorzendorf, two and a half miles northwest of Bunzlau, if this is not too far away. 11) Birkenbrück, one mile west-southwest of Bunzlau. 12) It is not known which place this might be. All these villages lie on the right bank of the Queis, within a mile of Naumburg.

The charter is quoted from a confirmation by Bernhard, Duke of Oppeln, Falkenberg, Strehlitz and Rosenberg, dated 10 November 1423.
